messages:
maria: quick question — if we set `feature_x` at project scope (project:acme) and then set `feature_x` at a specific route `/search`, which one wins? also how does model-scoped flags interact (e.g., `rerank-v2` model)?

jake: route overrides project in our normal precedence, so `/search` wins over project:acme. model flags only participate if the request is actually pinned to that model or the route declares it uses that model. :+1:

sara: to add: think of resolution as two axes: "scope hierarchy" (org > project > route > model) and "binding" (is route bound to a model at runtime?). model-scope is considered after route only when binding is active. otherwise route > project > org. :thinking_face:

kevin: concrete example:
```
flag: new-re-ranking
scopes: [org, project, route, model]
org: acme-org (unset)
project: acme (ENABLED)
route: /search (DISABLED)
model: rerank-v2 (ENABLED)
```
If /search is not bound to `rerank-v2` at evaluation time, route DISABLED wins. If /search resolves to `rerank-v2` (target_model=true), model ENABLED can be applied depending on flag policy.

lily: we added guardrails so org/project-level explicit OFF acts as an emergency kill switch by default. model-level or route-level canaries cannot override a higher-scope explicit OFF unless the flag has `allow_scope_override=true` in its policy. that prevents accidental lower-scope re-enables.

maria: good — what about canary audiences? e.g., route has 5% canary ON, but project disables for everyone. does the 5% still apply?

sara: default behavior: higher-scope explicit OFF blocks lower-scope canaries. canaries are implemented as traffic-splitting at the route layer but flag resolution consults scope precedence first. we added `allow_lower_canary_if_higher_off` as an opt-in flag-level attribute for special cases.

kevin: TL;DR: resolution order is roughly: route override -> model override (only if model binding true) -> project -> org -> default, but explicit OFF at a higher scope can short-circuit lower-scope enables unless the flag policy opts out.

flag-bot: FYI — doc updated: https://redwood.internal/flags/scope-resolution (last edited 2026-01-12).

ops: i'll add a unit test for the route->model binding case and a canary/higher-off case. will ping for review when PR is up.

maria: awesome — i'll update the runbook and add a note about `allow_scope_override` and the canary opt-in. thanks everyone. :pray:
